summaries.one_line: Software engineer and published researcher whose work spans embedded firmware, distributed data systems, applied machine learning, agentic LLM systems and education software; Master of Computer Science student at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.
summaries.short: Software engineer with experience at Qualcomm India (January 2023 - July 2026) on the Device Firmware Update team, including building agentic LLM tooling for defect triage; prior software engineering internships at Intel Solutions & Services India and Epsilon. Three peer-reviewed publications across computational biology, causal inference and document AI. Also builds the backend, database and LLM-powered analytics for Drona, a learning management and assessment platform, at Unifrost Eduverse, a three-member startup. B.E. in Computer Science from RV College of Engineering (GPA 9.22); enrolled in the Master of Computer Science program at UIUC since August 2026.
summaries.long: Abhay Harish Kashyap is a Master of Computer Science student at UIUC and a software engineer whose work spans embedded firmware, distributed data systems, applied machine learning and education software. At Qualcomm India he worked on the Device Firmware Update team from January 2023 to July 2026, joining as an Associate Engineer and being promoted to Software Engineer, where he owned SoC upgrade solutions, a data-relay mechanism and a core DFU refactor delivered across two major client releases, and made contributions to the upgrade framework used to deploy embedded ML models to hearable devices. He initiated agentic LLM tooling there, built with LangChain/LangGraph, CrewAI and Neo4j, that automated log analysis for defect triage. At Intel Solutions & Services India he worked in Customer Engineering on EV-telemetry JSON processing, cryptographic acceleration for a national stock exchange, and a Spark/Kubernetes/Kafka ETL pipeline. At Epsilon he benchmarked and optimized HBase, Apache Phoenix and Solr for large-scale retrieval. In parallel he led and published research: biomarker prediction for non-small cell lung cancer (Cancer Informatics), conditional independence testing on HPCC Systems with LexisNexis (JAIT), and deep-learning business-document recognition and table extraction (ICAIC 2025). He also led a Samsung Research Institute Bengaluru collaboration on instant-app technology that won an Excellence Award. At Unifrost Eduverse, a three-member startup, he is responsible for backend and database management for Drona, a learning management and assessment platform piloted at one public school in Bengaluru, and built its LLM-powered natural-language analytics assistant and a multi-agent engineering workflow with human approval.

technical_details.purpose: Scope academic, assessment and finance data to institutes.
technical_details.implementation_description: Prisma models carry tenant ownership and composite identifiers. executeWithTenant sets transaction-local app.current_tenant before queries. Migrations add PostgreSQL RLS policies and restricted runtime/platform roles; a separate platform client supports cross-tenant operations.
actions: Applied tenant context within database transactions.
Separated ordinary tenant queries, privileged platform operations and migration ownership.
material_limitations: Effective RLS depends on the deployed database role; owner/BYPASSRLS connections can bypass policies, and FORCE RLS/runtime-role assertions are not established.
Tenant isolation is an implementation intent, not a comprehensive security guarantee.

technical_details.purpose: Expose validated resource APIs and authenticated user context.
technical_details.implementation_description: Express resource routers share response/pagination helpers, asynchronous exception handling, database-error mapping and Zod/semantic checks. token access/refresh flows resolve student identities; middleware rechecks account activation and applies role/context policies. Jest/Supertest suites exercise routes against PostgreSQL.
actions: Standardized API responses and field/database error handling.
Connected account, role and student identity checks to request handling.
material_limitations: Validation and authorization are not uniform across all routes.
Refresh tokens lack server-side rotation/revocation; default-secret fallbacks and flag-controlled first-password enforcement remain hardening gaps.
Stricter login validation is in progress (not yet merged).

technical_details.purpose: Connect staff and student academic workflows through shared browser components.
technical_details.implementation_description: Next.js 16/React 19 portals cover enrollment, syllabus planning, lectures, attendance, assessments and fees. Resource API modules share bearer-token requests and field errors. Tailwind semantic tokens and Radix primitives support tables, dialogs and charts; KaTeX renders mathematics. Student CSV onboarding stages editable rows, validation and enrollment.
actions: Connected staff/student screens to academic and assessment resources.
Reused semantic tokens, responsive tables, dialogs and chart components.
Added formula rendering and row-level student-import feedback.
material_limitations: The browser client redirects on 401; stored refresh tokens do not establish transparent browser refresh.
Responsive/accessibility issues remain; the token audit does not prove WCAG conformance.
Student imports buffer input in memory; large-file behavior is not established.

technical_details.purpose: Assemble inspectable assessment drafts under authoring constraints.
technical_details.implementation_description: Question banks separate reusable content from test-item placement and marks. Templates and tag/topic eligibility feed seeded selection with a shared used-question set. Strict requests fail on shortfalls; non-strict requests return warnings/placeholders. Preview and item replacement precede confirmation; preview identity supports repeated-confirmation lookup.
actions: Modeled reusable questions and question/section/test templates.
Validated eligibility and selected questions against count/mark constraints.
Exposed draft preview, replacement and confirmation operations.
material_limitations: Selection uses existing questions and rules, not generative model authorship.
Preview lookup does not establish race-free exactly-once creation; non-strict placeholders must be resolved before participation.

technical_details.purpose: Coordinate assessment editing, scoring and released results.
technical_details.implementation_description: A shared lifecycle governs draft authoring, sealed structure, participation, evaluation and release. Online and OMR responses write common item scores/totals with bounded negative marks and protected manual overrides. Written-answer PDFs use presigned upload/completion and staff marking. Finalized score facts and interaction telemetry feed summaries and review screens.
actions: Applied state-dependent edit, participation and result-release gates.
Shared marking rules and preserved manual overrides during regrading.
Connected written submissions and finalized score/interaction summaries to staff review.
material_limitations: Written PDFs require manual evaluation; they are not automatically recognized or graded.
Declared upload metadata/key scope does not verify PDF bytes; telemetry does not establish exam integrity.
Mock student-list sparklines are excluded from real analytics claims; no learning gain is established. Legacy penalty cleanup is in progress (not yet merged).

technical_details.purpose: Share the student application while retaining native platform integrations.
technical_details.implementation_description: Kotlin Multiplatform separates domain, networking, storage and feature modules; Compose screens/ViewModels use Koin, Coroutines and StateFlow. Android and SwiftUI hosts embed the shared app. Ktor uses platform engines and bearer refresh. Portal/result views share behavior; Android Keystore-backed storage and iOS Keychain implement the token-store interface.
actions: Shared mobile screens, navigation, ViewModels and domain behavior.
Bound networking and credential storage to Android/iOS implementations.
Connected portal, written-upload and question-result review flows.
material_limitations: Implemented shared/iOS source does not establish App Store release or complete physical-device parity; migration/release checks remain open.
Native storage does not fix backend token revocation/rotation gaps; some iOS sign-out/payment-return checks remain open.

technical_details.purpose: Recover timed assessment state across interruptions and intermittent connectivity.
technical_details.implementation_description: Server APIs define start/end/grace windows and classify stale/invalid answer writes. A pure Kotlin reducer drives attempt transitions. AnswerBuffer persists interactions to Room before debounced/explicit flushes under a mutex; local/server state merges by saved timestamp with server ties winning. ServerClock anchors countdowns to server time plus monotonic elapsed time.
actions: Persisted answer changes before scheduling network flushes.
Reconciled local/server state on resume and separated stale/invalid writes.
Tested timing, answer merging and attempt transitions.
material_limitations: Recovery depends on server acceptance windows; lossless offline submission is not established.

The late-flush path trusts client timestamps and can alter submitted scores; bounded catch-up, finalized-state refusal and auditing are in progress (not yet merged), still with limited timestamp trust.
The clean-buffer heartbeat path and release-build/device recovery checks remain qualified.

technical_details.purpose: Record attempt interruptions through platform-specific proctoring bindings.
technical_details.implementation_description: Android integrates permission/service-readiness gates, screen pinning, secure-window controls, a foreground watchdog and durable interruption telemetry. Swift/Kotlin bridges connect iOS assessment sessions, capture/call signals and restart markers. iOS falls back to weaker telemetry controls when assessment-session capability is unavailable; staff review events through the attempt API.
actions: Added platform readiness gates, interruption signals and persisted event flushing.
Bridged iOS assessment/capture/call lifecycle behavior into shared Kotlin.
Kept explicit unproctored/fallback behavior distinct from stronger platform controls.
material_limitations: Soft proctoring does not establish cheating prevention or device-owner lockdown; OS/OEM restrictions affect behavior.
Apple entitlement approval, physical iPhone assessment/capture/call/reboot checks and TestFlight/App Store release remain open.
Earlier device reports do not establish post-migration release validation.

technical_details.purpose: Convert photographed paper responses into reviewable assessment scores.
technical_details.implementation_description: Printed ordering and template geometry align eligible MCQ rows. Browser capture/upload queues a Python FastAPI recognizer: OpenCV fiducial detection and four-point homography correct perspective, OMRChecker thresholds read bubbles, and blur/resolution/uncertainty checks flag problems. Stored reads feed later lifecycle-driven grading; staff corrections retain manual-override protection.
actions: Aligned printed question order, sheet geometry and score mapping.
Implemented perspective correction and threshold-based bubble recognition.
Separated capture, recognition, review and deferred grading.
material_limitations: Recognition is heuristic computer vision, not a trained model; confidence is not a calibrated probability. The 98% bubble-read accuracy is scoped to about 1,250 phone-captured images and does not establish general recognition accuracy.
Only the current 100-row single-sheet layout and eligible single-choice rows are evidenced; guided physical-phone capture remains unvalidated.
Upload/decode bounds and review photo access remain limited; local historical photo checks do not establish general device coverage.

technical_details.purpose: Turn natural-language requests into persistent analytical workspaces.
technical_details.implementation_description: The LLM planner receives schema/conversation context and emits QUERY, VISUALIZE and INSIGHT steps validated by Zod. An orchestrator executes steps and returns typed blocks. Redis scopes active state by tenant/user/session; PostgreSQL stores named snapshots/history. React/Recharts render tables, charts and insights with follow-up context, restore and error states.
actions: Validated structured execution plans before dispatch.
Connected follow-up prompts to prior workspace/query context.
Persisted saved views and rendered structured analytical blocks.
Engineered planner prompts with schema and conversation context to produce structured plans.
material_limitations: Provider integration/orchestration does not establish model training or analytical correctness.
Redis failure can interrupt session continuity; chart inference depends on data shape.
Teacher-scope and provider-context/data-minimization concerns remain; unrestricted access/privacy guarantees are not supported.

technical_details.purpose: Constrain model-generated SQL before tenant database execution.
technical_details.implementation_description: Implemented: SELECT parsing, top-level table-access checks, tenant-predicate/row-limit rewriting and a statement timeout. In progress (not yet merged): whole-AST traversal, nested/schema-qualified query rejection, function allowlisting, parenthesized predicates and read-only transactions with focused regression tests.
actions: Validated query shape and bounded result size/execution time.
Rewrote queries to enforce tenant predicates and row limits.
material_limitations: The implemented controls have known nested-expression and OR-precedence gaps that the in-progress changes address.
Isolation depends on deployed RLS/runtime roles; focused controls/tests do not establish comprehensive SQL safety.

technical_details.purpose: Account for AI usage, delivery failures and tenant budget settings.
technical_details.implementation_description: A common service normalizes Anthropic/OpenAI completions, token usage and request IDs. Decimal-based events/monthly aggregates distinguish provider cost, billable delivery and absorbed failures; requests become billable after delivery. Tenant settings and pre-request usage checks expose enablement, budget/overage thresholds and operator/tenant usage views.
actions: Recorded per-call usage, aggregate costs and failure stages.
Marked delivered results billable separately from incurred provider cost.
Connected quota settings and operator controls to tenant usage screens.
material_limitations: Configured prices are accounting inputs; actual spend, savings and billing reconciliation are unconfirmed.
Caps use billable cost, exclude absorbed failed-request cost and lack concurrent reservations; they are not strict provider-spend bounds.

technical_details.purpose: Build question-bank data with provenance and resumable verification.
technical_details.implementation_description: Playwright captures rendered exam questions for Claude Code vision-assisted transcription into CSV/LaTeX. Manifests retain source/row identity and verification states; separate sessions compare transcription and captured answer keys. Shared linting, locked JSONL updates, image review and recapture support recovery. A transaction covering accepted question rows and tags before asynchronous image jobs is in progress (not yet merged).
actions: Separated capture, agent transcription, verification and flagged-row resolution.
Validated structured rows/math and serialized manifest updates.
material_limitations: An agent reads screenshots; the scripts are not autonomous OCR, and verified status does not establish measured transcription accuracy.
Transactional import is in progress (not yet merged) and covers accepted database rows/tags, not rejected rows or asynchronous images. Repeated successful uploads can duplicate data.
Dataset/fixture counts and staging notes are not confirmed adoption or throughput metrics.

technical_details.purpose: Separate background processing and communications from request handling.
technical_details.implementation_description: Typed BullMQ handlers run in a separate worker over Redis with retry/backoff/failure retention and cluster-compatible key prefixes. Schedules and lifecycle hooks drive reminders, OMR and report/image jobs; notification records retain recipient status. Nodemailer/SMTP and Twilio adapters share an opt-in test-only delivery sink that avoids real sends.
actions: Registered typed workers and repeatable/lifecycle-triggered jobs.
Centralized provider delivery and observable test-only output.
material_limitations: Reminder job IDs contain unsupported colon patterns; the ID/drift fix is in progress (not yet merged).
Development JSON transport and the test sink do not establish live delivery, throughput or success rates.

technical_details.purpose: Connect fee obligations, payment review and supporting object storage.
technical_details.implementation_description: Batch configurations, student fees and dated installments feed staff/student views. UPI claims retain reference/photo evidence and staff verification/void states with conflict checks. PhonePe code initiates sessions, polls and verifies callback signatures; tenant secrets use AES-256-GCM. Shared S3 helpers store evidence and issue signed upload/download URLs.
actions: Connected fee balances and installment states to staff/student actions.
Added claim verification, settlement conflict checks and encrypted payment settings.
Centralized object operations and signed URLs for uploaded evidence.
material_limitations: PhonePe callbacks are currently blocked by router authentication; signature code does not establish working end-to-end settlement or merchant activation.
Authorization/numeric validation, settlement concurrency, amount/merchant checks and key rotation remain qualified; no revenue or accounting-completeness claim is supported.
Object ownership, declared-size enforcement and external-image SSRF concerns prevent a comprehensive storage-safety claim.

technical_details.purpose: Host the pilot and document recovery and repeatable onboarding.
technical_details.implementation_description: The pilot ran on Supabase PostgreSQL with Vercel and Railway hosting. Local tooling uses Docker-backed PostgreSQL, pg_dump snapshots/restores, reproducible academic/mobile seeds and an S3-compatible endpoint. AWS templates/runbooks describe EC2 API/worker processes behind Nginx/systemd with ElastiCache Redis as an alternative deployment. Onboarding sequences tenant/admin setup, syllabus, imports and enrollment. An AWS test-VM configuration supports agent testing.
actions: Documented runtime versus migration connections and API/worker deployment.
Provided local database snapshots/restores and targeted test fixtures.
Sequenced tenant setup, syllabus/question imports and enrollment.
Used AWS EC2 for development; production pilot hosting ran on Supabase PostgreSQL, Vercel and Railway.
material_limitations: AWS EC2/ElastiCache exist as configuration and runbooks only; no AWS deployment is established.
No successful restoration, disaster recovery or availability is established.
Some seed paths reset demo tenants; fixtures are not real institutions/users and are not safe production onboarding by default.

technical_details.purpose: Coordinate agent changes with persistent human decisions and guarded integration.
technical_details.implementation_description: Claude Code reporter/fixer/QA/tester roles progress bugs through a resumable Markdown ledger under time/usage limits. Human decisions and Git-history provenance release work. Linux permissions and a push guard enforce role/path boundaries and coordinated API/spec checks. A Python/Tkinter review app displays evidence, saves decisions atomically and reapplies bug-ID decisions with backups during Git conflicts.
actions: Orchestrated bug reporting, approved fixes, test maintenance and independent verification.
Enforced approval provenance and role-specific integration boundaries outside prompts.
Built evidence review and durable human-decision synchronization.
material_limitations: Approval/push controls do not establish complete sandboxing; credential/environment exposure concerns remain.
Historical runs do not establish measured productivity or defect reduction; CLI authentication/usage limits affect operation.
The desktop app is ad-hoc signed and not notarized for general distribution.

technical_details.purpose: Keep specifications, API contracts and behavioral checks aligned across surfaces.
technical_details.implementation_description: OpenSpec designs/tasks and Claude/Cursor instructions accompany a versioned OpenAPI repository consumed through submodules. Route/spec and operation-ownership checks complement backend PostgreSQL tests, web builds/Playwright journeys and mobile Kotlin/Android/iOS checks. Shipping scripts gate the final commit. A separate source-blind bubblewrap observer follows persona journeys and retains screenshots/friction evidence.
actions: Connected specifications, task artifacts and API contracts to implementation checks.
Prepared repository-specific build/test gates and final-commit integration checks.
Added a source-blind observer path with retained user-journey evidence.
integration_points: Human PRs and agent push guard
material_limitations: Archived tasks and gate configuration do not establish completed verification or currently passing builds/tests; guide/submodule versions can drift.
Cold-observer networking is shared for local testing, leaving residual local database reachability; some cross-surface/device acceptance remains open.
No complete acceptance pass or measured usability improvement is established.

metadata.role_optimization: none - this file is role-neutral by design. Section and array ordering carries no emphasis. Do not infer that earlier entries are more important.
generation_directives: This file contains facts, not bullets. Synthesize bullet points at generation time from `situation`, `constraints`, `actions`, `technologies_used`, `metrics`, `outcomes` and optional `technical_details`. Never copy a field verbatim as a resume line.
Omit unavailable values from generated prose. Never invent dates, measurements or named entities to fill null fields; retain recorded qualitative outcomes without adding quantities.

A general skill listing does not establish use in an engagement. Write experience and project bullets from the technologies and activities recorded for that engagement, applying explicit shared facts only within their stated scope.
Entries under basics.stated_interests are stated aspirations. They may inform a cover letter or summary but must never be presented as accomplishments.

Use technical_details as supporting facts for their parent project, retaining implementation_status, material_limitations and metric scope. Distinguish implemented work, work in progress (not yet merged), deployment configuration, confirmed pilot use and measured outcomes; code or configuration alone does not establish live operation, completed releases, security guarantees or broader impact.

confidentiality.rule: Client names are not disclosed and must remain abstracted as 'two major clients'.
Specific SoC part numbers, internal module names and internal tool names are not recorded here and must not be invented.
Both Intel customer identities are withheld as private information. Refer to them only as 'an electric vehicle manufacturer' and 'a national stock exchange'. Do not name or infer them.
Work authorization status must never appear in the resume body. It exists only to answer application-form questions.

maintenance.how_to_extend: Add a new engagement as an object under work[].projects[] (if it happened at an employer) or under projects[] (if it did not), using the same field shape and a stable id. Record technologies_used on the engagement and add any relevant general skills as objects with a name and an optional factual note. Store project actions[], employer working_practices[], and basics.stated_interests.items[] as arrays of strings. Store text-only project outcomes[] entries as strings; retain an object when an outcome carries additional metadata such as award_ref. Optional technical_details remain nested under their parent project, retain stable IDs, and record implementation status and material limitations.
maintenance.invariant: Every stated metric, date and named entity must be candidate-confirmed. Unavailable details may be omitted or left null and must not be inferred. Resolve questions with the candidate before adding facts to this record.
